transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the Florida coast.
The Associated Press capturing the winds picking up Panama City
hours before the storm is projected to make landfall tonight
on the northern Gulf Coast along the Florida-Alabama border.
The hurricane has grown to a cat-3 with 120 mph winds.
Dozens of counties are under a state of emergency in Florida and Alabama.
In Mobile, Mayor Spiro Chiragatas says the city is working to guard
against serious damage from potential floods.
We are constantly trying to improve our storm water system
and so over the last few days we've been focusing on that,
making sure that we're cleaning out our drainage ditches
and all our channels to move this water off of our city, off of our streets.
The mayor is speaking to ABC News.
Secretary of Homeland Security Mark Wayne Mullen says
ICE officers did not know a five-year-old boy was in the car
when they surrounded and shot a Dominican man in New York City Thursday night.
NPR's Nate Perez reports officers fired as many as seven rounds.
ICE shot Oscar Belgall in the neck when he was pulling into a parking space.
Mullen says ICE wasn't aware a child was in the car,
but he says that Belgall accelerated his speed and ramped two vehicles.
Mullen also alleges Belgall appeared to target officers with his car.
The public outcry should be also towards this criminal,
this thug, this gangbanger, this possible murderer.
Belgall was treated at a hospital,
but has been moved to a detention center outside New York.
New York Mayor Zoran Mamdani and Governor Kathy Hochul denounced ICE
and demanded they pause their operations.
But Mullen has vowed to continue.
Nate Perez, NPR News.
Vice President J.D. Vance says he does not know if the Pentagon will move ahead
with the livestream of the execution of former Army psychiatrist Nidal Malik Hassan,
who carried out a shooting rampage that killed 13 people at the Fort Hood military base in 2009.
Vance told reporters today, quote, "I don't know that that's actually going to happen,"
adding, quote, "I'm not going to be watching it."
NPR's Jason DeRose reports Catholic bishops in the U.S.
are condemning the Trump administration's plan.
The president of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops,
Archbishop Paul Coakley of Oklahoma City, writes in a public statement
that he learned of the Defense Department's plan with, quote, "shock and great sorrow."
The execution by firing squad is scheduled to take place December 3rd.
Coakley writes that in no way can Nidal Hassan's killing of 13 people be condoned,
but a livestreamed execution is a, quote, "barbaric promotion of a culture of death."
He points to a passage from the New Testament letter to the Romans, quote,
"Do not repay anyone evil for evil."
Coakley says the public execution, even of one who's done grave harm,
will only further undermine the moral fabric of our nation.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
British counterterrorism police say they have arrested and released two men
for trespassing at a military base in England that is used by U.S. and NATO troops.
It is the second such incident in the past two weeks, as NPR's Lauren Freya reports from London.
The latest two suspects are Latvian nationals.
Counterterrorism police say the men breached the perimeter of a royal air force
based north of London in the middle of the night Wednesday into Thursday.
It has since been released on bail but remain under investigation for alleged trespassing,
criminal damage and possible national security violations.
This was at RAF Molesworth, a different base from RAF Fairford,
where U.S. bombers used to take off for attacks on Iran before the planes were relocated
after another security breach and what British police describe as an investigation
into a possible Iran-linked terror plot.
Authorities say they're aware of heightened interest in these breaches,
but that there is no indication that they are connected.
Lauren Freya, NPR News, London.
Authorities in Russia say they have lifted all public health restrictions
following the death of a 28-year-old lab worker at a plague research institute in Siberia.
The legendary former NFL coach and player Mike Ditka has died.
A family spokesperson says Ditka died this morning surrounded by family and friends.
He was 86.
Hall of Famer played on the Bears' 1963 NFL championship team
and coached the Bears to their only Super Bowl championship after the 1985 season.
He is being remembered as a larger-than-life personality beloved by generation of Bears fans.
It's NPR.
